questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors
questions.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -5 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -5 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & -4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & -4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
k=0.
$$

evidence.solution_quote:
Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
k=0.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors
questions.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2 \\ -6\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7 \\ 18\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -10 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7 \\ 18\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -10 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=-12 \\ -2{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}=-10 \\ -6{x}_{1}+18{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & -12 \\ -2 & 7 & -10 \\ -6 & 18 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 4 \\ -2 & 7 & -10 \\ -6 & 18 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -6 & 18 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & k+24\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k+24.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k+24\,⇒\,k=-24.
$$

evidence.solution_quote:
Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k+24\,⇒\,k=-24.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether a Vector Lies on a Plane
questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,-4,2⟩$, $c=⟨3,-10,2⟩$, and  $u=⟨-2,5,0⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -10 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s+3t=-2 \\ -4s-10t=5 \\ 2s+2t=0\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ -4 & -10 & 5 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=-2,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $s$ and $t$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc=u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $u$ does *not* lie on the plane $Π.$

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, we conclude that $u$ does *not* lie on the plane $Π.$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether a Vector Lies on a Plane
questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,-1,3⟩$, $c=⟨-2,4,-3⟩$, and  $u=⟨3,-7,3⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s-2t=3 \\ -s+4t=-7 \\ 3s-3t=3\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -7 \\ 3 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s-2t=3 \\ t=-2 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=-2.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s-2t & =3 \\ s-2(-2) & =3 \\ s+4 & =3 \\ s & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-1,\,t=-2,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-b-2c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-1)\cdot (-2)=2.$

evidence.solution_quote:
Since we found a solution $s=-1,\,t=-2,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-b-2c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-1)\cdot (-2)=2.$
